h: Torah Heals the Past and Prepares Yisrael for Lasting Renewal

p: "Heal me, Hashem, and I shall be healed, etc."
This is because there are sins
such as the blemish of the bris
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר חֵלֶק א רִיט, ב)
and we have said that this is
but Torah, which comes forth from Chochmah
"and a healing to all his flesh."
and in the opposite case "flesh of donkeys."
And this is along the lines of what they said
"Through sacrifice and offering he is not atoned,
but he is atoned through Torah."
HaKadosh Baruch Hu is called Torah
"'When I call out the Name of Hashem,
as referring to the berachah before the Torah."
And this is what it says:
"Heal me, Hashem, and I shall be healed"
"and I shall be healed" in the future.
grows strong and renews itself every day,
and were it not that HaKadosh Baruch Hu
and when the past is rectified,
one merits the help of Hashem Yisbarach
"Save me, and I shall be saved"
along the lines of what they said
(מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה אַחֲרֵי, וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כא, ד)
And this is what it says:
"and I shall be saved" in the future,
as stated in the holy Zohar
and David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
who was a chariot for this middah,
and my mouth shall declare Your praise" — precisely.
And the Men of the Great Assembly
instituted this text in the tefillah,
from the singular to the plural.
did not say it about himself
כִּי אִם עַל כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלּוֹ
but about all of Klal Yisrael,
from the wording of the verses.
אַךְ הִיא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
But it follows what is stated
on the difference between the Ten Commandments,
which were said in the singular,
while in Kedoshim they were repeated
the Ten Commandments in the plural;
with one heart and one will
when they stood at Mount Sinai;
That is: at Matan Torah it is written,
as they said in the Mechilta;
and then they merited Matan Torah
and the Ten Commandments in the singular.
when they were repeated in the Ohel Moed,
when they were not in that one will.
of when we will merit the holiness
when we say, "the time of the giving of our Torah,"
for then is the time to merit
the holiness of the first Tablets,
the learning of Torah was implanted in their hearts,
and with the utterance "You shall not have"
the yetzer hara was uprooted from them
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת יִשָּׁקֵנִי)
(as they said, Shir HaShirim Rabbah on "Let him kiss me," 1:2);
and to merit the rectification of everything,
that they would not have died
the yetzer hara and the Angel of Death,
as one man with one heart,
since not all are as one man
And this is the connection of the haftorah
as the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote;
which are a semblance of Olam Haba,
which is one-sixtieth of Olam Haba
which are as the addition to Shabbos
from the day that is entirely Shabbos,
are more a semblance of Olam Haba
we read as haftorah with this parsha
a passage that points to the rectification
And it is a preparation for Shavuos,
so that the year may end with its curses";
וַעֲצֶרֶת נַמִּי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הִיא כּוּלֵּי
"and Atzeres too is a Rosh Hashanah, etc."
and a year begin with its blessings.
